title: Sales and Negotiation Skills
summary: Learn consultative selling: the sales process, pipelines and forecasts, discovery questions and value-based presentations, handling objections, negotiation with BATNA and ZOPA, closing and ethical account management.
audience: Sales staff, entrepreneurs, traders, freelancers and anyone who negotiates

body.p: Selling is helping customers make a good decision to buy something that solves their problem. Modern professional selling is consultative: you listen first, understand the need, then show how your product helps. Pushy selling may win one sale but loses trust and referrals.

steps: Prospect: find people or businesses who might need what you sell.
Qualify: check they have the need, budget, authority to decide and a timeline.
Discover: ask questions to understand their situation and priorities.
Present: show how your solution meets their specific needs.
Close: ask for the decision and agree next steps.
Follow up: deliver, check satisfaction and build the relationship.

body.p: The process applies to a market trader selling phones, a pharmaceutical representative visiting clinics and a software firm selling to banks; the scale differs, the principles do not.

body.tip: Prepare before every meeting: know the customer's business, likely needs and the one outcome you want from the conversation.

body.p: A sales pipeline shows every potential deal and its stage. Tracking it lets you forecast sales and see where deals get stuck.

Suppose 20% of leads become qualified prospects and 25% of those close. From 200 leads: 200 x 0.20 = 40 prospects, and 40 x 0.25 = 10 sales. At R8000 per sale that is R80 000. To reach R120 000 you need 120 000 / 8000 = 15 sales, which needs 15 / 0.25 = 60 prospects and 60 / 0.20 = 300 leads, or better conversion rates.
Multiply each deal by its probability of closing. Deals of R50 000 at 60%, R20 000 at 30% and R10 000 at 10% give an expected R30 000 + R6000 + R1000 = R37 000.

list: Prospect from referrals, existing customers, events, LinkedIn and partnerships.
Record every contact and next step in a customer relationship management (CRM) tool or simple spreadsheet.
Remove dead deals honestly so the forecast stays real.

body.tip: Ask every happy customer for one referral; referred prospects usually convert far better than cold contacts.

body.p: Great salespeople talk less and ask more. Good questions help the customer see their own problem clearly and want to solve it.

list: Situation: "How do you record stock today?"
Problem: "What happens when stock runs out?"
Implication: "How much do those lost sales cost you each month?"
Need-payoff: "If you always knew stock levels, what would that mean for the business?"

body.p: This sequence (often called SPIN) moves from facts to the cost of the problem to the value of fixing it, so the customer explains the benefit in their own words.

list: Link each feature to a benefit the customer said they care about: "Automatic alerts mean you never miss a reorder."
Use evidence: demonstrations, case studies, testimonials with permission, trial periods.
Quantify value: time saved, costs cut, sales gained.
Keep it short and check understanding often.

body.tip: If you cannot link a feature to something the customer told you, leave it out.

body.p: Objections are normal; they often mean the customer is interested but has a concern. Treat them as questions to answer, not attacks.

steps: Acknowledge the concern: "I understand budget is tight this quarter."
Clarify: "Is the total price the issue, or the upfront payment?"
Respond with relevant information, options or evidence.

list: Price: show value and total cost, offer payment terms or a smaller package; avoid jumping straight to a discount.
Timing: find out what is driving the delay and agree a specific follow-up date.
Trust: offer references, guarantees or a pilot.
Competitor: compare fairly on the customer's priorities; never insult competitors.

body.p: Discounts are expensive. If a product costs R70 and sells for R100 (R30 profit), a 10% discount cuts profit to R20 per unit, so you must sell 30 / 20 = 1.5 times as many units, 50% more, just to earn the same.

body.tip: Keep a list of the objections you hear most and prepare tested answers to each.

body.p: Negotiation is reaching an agreement when both sides have different interests. Good negotiators prepare thoroughly and look for deals that leave both sides better off.

list: BATNA: your best alternative to a negotiated agreement. A strong alternative gives you power to walk away.
Reservation point: your walk-away price.

ZOPA (zone of possible agreement): the overlap between the parties' limits. If a seller will accept no less than R70 000 and a buyer will pay up to R85 000, the ZOPA is R70 000 to R85 000, a range of R15 000.
Anchoring: the first number often shapes the outcome, so open with a well-justified offer.
Interests versus positions: "I want R80 000" is a position; "I need cash before the school term" is an interest that might be met in other ways, such as faster payment.
Never give a concession without getting something back: "If you pay upfront, I can include delivery."
Make concessions smaller as you go, signalling that you are near your limit.
Trade things that are cheap for you but valuable to them.
Summarise agreements in writing at the end.

body.tip: Prepare your BATNA, your reservation point and your opening offer before you start, and do not reveal your walk-away point.

body.p: Closing is simply asking for a decision once the customer's needs are met. Summarise the agreed benefits, then ask directly: "Shall we start delivery on Monday?" If they hesitate, there is an unanswered concern; return to discovery.

list: Deliver exactly what was promised, on time.
Check in after delivery to make sure the customer is getting value.
Solve problems fast; a well-handled complaint can increase loyalty.
Look for further needs and ask for referrals and reviews.
Key accounts (your largest customers) deserve regular reviews and planning together.
Never lie, exaggerate or hide fees and conditions.
Do not pressure vulnerable customers or sell things they do not need.
Refuse and report bribes; anti-corruption laws apply to private and public sales.
Protect customer data and respect requests not to be contacted.

body.tip: Measure your success partly by repeat customers and referrals; they show whether you sold honestly.

options: Understanding the customer's needs before proposing a solution

quiz.q: 200 leads, 20% qualify, 25% of those close. How many sales?
To make 15 sales with 20% and 25% conversion rates, how many leads are needed?
Deals of R50 000 (60%), R20 000 (30%) and R10 000 (10%) give a weighted forecast of:
"How much do stock-outs cost you each month?" is which SPIN question?
What should you link each feature to?
options: A benefit the customer cares about

quiz.q: The first step in handling an objection is to:
Cost R70, price R100. After a 10% discount, how much more must you sell to earn the same profit?

options: Your best alternative if no agreement is reached

quiz.q: Seller minimum R70 000, buyer maximum R85 000. The ZOPA is:
"If you pay upfront, I can include delivery" is an example of:
A customer hesitates when asked to decide. What does this usually mean?
options: You should cut the price immediately
Hiding compulsory fees until after signing
Respecting a request not to be contacted
